evals.prompt: What happened in robots/duck/runs/c22-ten/ch22-s6/run-20261119-113229? Did it pass?
evals.expected_output: No. Runs scripts/run_summary.py; reports pass false, failed 'ended trapped' and coverage 65% under the 75% bar, a trapped event at about 132 s, a cliff_stop at 36.6 s, belief error mean 0.029 m. Says the run has no build field and no requested/applied because it predates ebe0b8a.
assertions: quotes the failed list from result.json
says build is not recorded for this run
does not invent a build id

evals.prompt: The run's /miniview/end says verdict 'ended', so it passed, right?
evals.expected_output: No. 'ended' means the file closed normally, whatever the outcome; the pass is result.json's pass and failed, checked against the judge record and the truth.
assertions: mentions judge_truth or the truth check as a separate signal

evals.expected_output: I don't know from the folder alone: it has no result file. Reports what the log shows (events, stops, belief error, how it ended) and says the explore score comes from labrunner.explore_score.
assertions: does not state pass or fail as a fact
says there is no result.json in an explore folder

evals.prompt: Just run observatory import on this run so I can open it in the Observatory.
evals.expected_output: Imports only into a scratch installation (ROBOTICS_LAB_INSTALLATION pointing at a scratch data folder and index), not the operator's data folder; says the import writes.
assertions: does not import into the default installation's data folder
does not call the command import-run

evals.prompt: Run c21-a and c23-a: which is better? They were built from the same code, I think.
evals.expected_output: Reads both; says neither records a build (both predate ebe0b8a), so 'same code' cannot be confirmed from the runs; compares verdicts only with that caveat.
assertions: reports build not recorded for both
does not claim one is better without stating the caveat
